pages: Thawan was cleaning the attic when he found an old box.
Inside the box was a yellow piece of paper. It was a map!
"Look at this!" he shouted. "It is a treasure map of our neighborhood!"
He called Nong Fah and Ollie right away.
The first clue said: "Start at the tallest tree."
They ran to the big mango tree by the pond.
The next clue said: "Walk ten steps to the yellow flowers."
Nong Fah counted the steps. One, two, three… ten!
"Now dig by the white stone," read Ollie.
They dug and dug. Suddenly, Thawan's shovel hit something hard!
It was a small metal box. Inside were old photos and a little toy car.
"These are Grandpa's things from when he was a boy!" said Thawan.
They looked at every photo and laughed all afternoon.
The best treasure is not gold. It is remembering the people we love.
Little Duck had a problem. All the other ducks could fly, but she could not.
"I am scared," she told Ollie. "What if I fall?"
"Everyone is scared at first," said Ollie. "I will teach you."
First, they practiced flapping. Flap, flap, flap!
"Good!" said Ollie. "Now try a little jump."
Duck jumped off a small rock. She landed on her feet.
Next, she jumped from a bigger rock. Her wings held her up for one second!
Every day, Duck practiced with Ollie.
Some days she fell into the soft grass. But she always got up.
Then one morning, Duck flapped her wings and did not come down.
"I am flying!" she shouted. "Ollie, look! I am really flying!"
She flew in a big circle around the pond.
Big things do not happen in one day. They happen a little bit at a time.
On Saturday night, the friends went to the night market.
The market was full of lights, music, and wonderful smells.
"Look at all the food!" said Thawan. There was grilled chicken, mango sticky rice, and fruit smoothies.
Nong Fah held her little purse tightly. She had saved her coins for three weeks.
"What will you buy?" asked Ollie. "Candy? A toy?"
"It is a secret," Nong Fah smiled.
They walked past a stall with beautiful hair bows. Nong Fah loved bows. But she did not stop.
They walked past a stall with sweet coconut cakes. Nong Fah loved cakes. But she did not stop.
Finally, she found the right stall. It sold soft, warm scarves.
She picked a blue one and paid with all her coins.
"A scarf?" asked Thawan. "But it is not for me," said Nong Fah.
"Tomorrow is my mom's birthday. She always gives me everything. Tonight, I wanted to give something back."
Ollie smiled a big smile. "That is the best thing at this whole market."
And when her mom opened the gift the next day, she hugged Nong Fah for a very long time.
The science fair was in one week.
"Let's make a volcano!" said Thawan. "A real one that erupts!"
He and Nong Fah built a mountain out of paper and clay.
They painted it brown and red. It looked amazing.
On testing day, they poured in the special mix. Everyone waited.
Nothing happened. Not even one bubble.
"Oh no," said Thawan. "Our volcano is broken."
"It is not broken," said Nong Fah. "We just made a mistake somewhere. Let's find it."
They checked their notes. They had forgotten the most important thing — the vinegar!
They tried again. This time, orange foam bubbled up and poured down the mountain!
"It works! It really works!" they cheered.
At the science fair, their volcano erupted perfectly three times.
They won a blue ribbon for teamwork.
A mistake is not the end. It is just a step on the way to getting it right.
One sunny morning, Cat saw that the gate was open.
"I will just look outside for one minute," she thought.
She followed a butterfly down the street. Then she chased a leaf around the corner.
She sniffed the flowers by the school. She napped on a warm rock.
But when she woke up, the sun was going down.
Cat looked around. Nothing looked like home. She was lost!
Back at the house, Nong Fah was worried. "Cat! Where are you?"
Thawan looked down the street. Ollie flew high above the houses.
"I see her!" Ollie called. "She is by the school!"
Cat heard a familiar sound. "Cat! Cat!" It was Nong Fah's voice!
She ran toward the voice as fast as her legs could go.
Nong Fah picked her up and held her close. "You scared me, silly Cat."
That night, Cat curled up in her own warm basket.
Adventures are fun, she thought, but coming home is the best part.
The rainy season had come. Rain fell all week long.
Little rivers of water ran down the sides of the street.
"I know a game," said Thawan. "Let's race paper boats!"
They folded boats out of colored paper. Thawan's was red. Nong Fah's was yellow. Ollie's was blue.
"Ready, set, go!" They dropped their boats into the water.
The boats raced down the street, faster and faster.
Thawan's red boat took the lead! But then it got stuck on a stick.
Nong Fah's yellow boat spun in a circle. "Go, boat, go!" she laughed.
Ollie's blue boat sailed past them both, smooth and steady.
At the finish line, the blue boat came in first.
"The slow and steady boat won the race!" said Ollie proudly.
They raced boats until the rain stopped and the sun came out.
Rainy days are not bad days. They are just different kinds of good days.
The kite festival was coming to town.
"First prize is a golden trophy," said Thawan. "I am going to win it."
He did not buy a kite. He made one himself.
He used bamboo sticks, bright paper, and a long tail of ribbons.
He worked on it for five days. It was shaped like a bird.
On festival day, the sky was full of kites. Big kites, small kites, dragon kites!
Thawan's bird kite flew high and danced in the wind.
But another kite flew even higher — a giant butterfly kite.
The butterfly kite won the golden trophy. Thawan got second place.
For a minute, Thawan felt sad. He had worked so hard.
Then a little boy walked up. "Your bird kite was my favorite," he said. "Can you teach me to make one?"
Thawan smiled. They sat down together with sticks and paper.
And teaching that little boy felt better than any trophy.
Sometimes second place gives you something first place cannot.
Grandma's birthday was tomorrow, and Ollie wanted to bake her a special cake.
He found a fancy recipe with three layers and pink frosting.
"Easy," said Ollie. It was not easy.
First, he dropped an egg on the floor. Splat!
Then he opened the flour bag too fast. A white cloud filled the kitchen!
The first layer burned. The second layer fell apart.
Ollie sat down in the messy kitchen. Flour covered his glasses.
"I cannot make a fancy cake," he sighed.
Then he had an idea. "But I can make a simple one."
He baked one small, simple cake and wrote "I love you" on top with frosting.
At the party, Grandma took one bite and her eyes filled with happy tears.
"This is the most delicious cake I have ever eaten," she said.
A gift made with love does not need to be fancy. It just needs to be yours.
The class took a trip to the zoo.
They saw lions, penguins, and monkeys swinging from ropes.
Then they came to the sloth. He hung from his tree and did not move.
"Is he sleeping?" asked Thawan. "Is he frozen?" asked Nong Fah.
They waved. The sloth did not wave back.
They sang a song. The sloth slowly blinked one eye.
"He is so boring," said Thawan. "Let's go see the elephants."
"Wait," said Nong Fah. "Let's just watch him quietly."
They stood very still and watched.
Slowly, slowly, the sloth reached for a leaf. Slowly, slowly, he ate it.
Then he turned his head and gave them a slow, sleepy smile.
"He smiled at us!" whispered Thawan. "He is not boring. He is just... unhurried."
Some friends are fast and some are slow. If you wait patiently, every animal has something to show you.
It was the hottest day of summer.
"Everyone is thirsty today," said Nong Fah. "Let's open a smoothie stand!"
They picked ripe mangoes from the tree. Ollie mixed them with ice.
Thawan painted a sign with a big yellow mango on it.
They set up a little table by the street.
Their first customer bought two smoothies. "Delicious!" she said.
Soon there was a line! The friends worked as a team.
Nong Fah took the money and counted the change carefully.
Then an old mail carrier walked by, hot and tired from his long day.
He looked at the smoothies, then at the coins in his hand. He did not have enough.
"This one is free," said Nong Fah, handing him the biggest smoothie.
"You work hard for everyone," said Thawan. "Today we can work for you."
At the end of the day, they counted their money — and their happy customers.
They earned many coins, but the mail carrier's smile was worth the most.
